## Part 2 — What the change is, and why

### 1. `pipeline/src/run.ts` — new source in `RSS_SOURCES`

```ts
{ url: "https://www.gp.se/rss", publisher: "Göteborgs-Posten" }
```

Added for **regional/local Häcken coverage** that the national sports feeds
structurally cannot carry. The in-code comment documents two verified traps:

- **The server serves GZIP while declaring `content-type: text/xml`.** A naive
  `<rss` marker check sees binary and falsely reports "0 RSS markers" — a
  false soft-404 negative. Any future validation must decompress first.
- **Yield is low: 3 of 45 items mention Häcken.** This is the front-page feed.
  No sport feed exists (`/sport.rss`→404, `/sport/feed`→410,
  `/arkiv/sport.rss`→404), so the front page is the only option. It contributes
  local coach/supporter press, not article volume. Do not "fix" this later by
  expecting density — the trade-off is intentional and documented.

`"Göteborgs-Posten"` **already exists** in `PUBLISHER_ROLES` in
`newsEvents.ts` as `"secondary"` with the comment *"local reporting on
Gothenburg clubs"*. No role wiring is needed. Do not add it.

### 2. `docs/SOURCES.md` — source audit corrections

- **Göteborgs-Posten**: confirmed working — HTTP 200, `text/xml`, 45 items,
  freshest `pubDate` 2026-09-30 19:22 GMT, verified via the real
  `fetchRss()` (`ok:true`, `items:45`).
- **Fotbolltransfers — CORRECTION, do not revert.** This row previously said
  *"Ingent fungerande flöde"* (no working feed). That was already disproven:
  the working URL is `/rss/klubbar/27`, which is why the source appears in
  `RSS_SOURCES` today. The audit was stale and the row has been corrected.
- **Fotbollskanalen**: added a 2026-09-30 re-check row confirming there is
  **still no feed**. Every candidate (`/min-feed`, `?feed=rss2`, `?feed=atom`,
  `?rss`, `/arkiv`, `/rssfeed`) returns HTTP 200 with Next.js HTML and zero
  items. `/min-feed` is declared as an `href` in the page, which is why it
  looks promising — it is a web page, not a feed. The site is Next.js/Sanity.
  **Getting this source requires scraping, not a feed.** Out of scope here.

# Part 4 — Deploy facts (already established — trust these)

| Question | Answer | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Does push to `main` run the Gemini pipeline? | **No** | `deploy.yml`: checkout → `npm ci` → typecheck+test → build → upload-pages-artifact → deploy-pages. No pipeline step. |
| Does `ci.yml` run Gemini? | **No** | It runs `pipeline:validate` (validates the *existing* `app.json`), not `npm run pipeline`. |
| Gemini cost of this push | **Zero** | Neither workflow references `GEMINI_API_KEY`. |
| Is `app.json` regenerated? | **No** | Nothing regenerates it; it is built as committed. |
| What changes in production? | **Only JS/CSS** | `RSS_SOURCES` is pipeline-side and never enters the bundle. |

**Consequence:** production will be byte-identical for all user-visible code.
The new feed has **no effect until the next `data-update.yml` nightly run**
(cron `30 3 * * *`), and then only if Gemini is available.

> **This is exactly the failure mode from `AGENTS.md` §1–§3: a green deploy
> proves nothing about whether data changed.** The deploy being user-invisible
> is the *expected* result here, not a defect. Do not "fix" it.
